data.name: Dragonflight
data.detailed_description: Dragonflight VR is a multi-level VR experience featuring massive, destructible environments, fast-paced combat with enemy dragons swarming the skies around you, ancient castles teeming with archers, and lost wizard towers shrouded in mist. Ride your dragon over mountainous countryside, through showers of flaming arrows, and then deep into canyons where huge dragons rule. The only way to get a more realistic feeling of riding a dragon than Dragonflight VR would be to breed one!

data.short_description: Feel the thrill of riding on your very own dragon in virtual reality. Produced by the academy award winning cinematic CGI masters behind The Matrix, Life of Pi, Hunger Games, Harry Potter, Zootopia, Snow White & the Huntsman.

reviews.review:
Dragonflight is a free VR game that gives me a pretty simple fantasy. I get to ride a dragon and fly around a large fantasy world while fighting other dragons and attacking things on the ground. It is not a full RPG and there is no huge story for me to get invested in. It is much closer to a short VR action experience that is mainly trying to make riding a dragon feel exciting. I think that basic idea works pretty well, especially when I am actually in the air and moving quickly through the environment.

The flying is easily the best part for me. I can steer the dragon through mountains and valleys, fly around castles and move through areas filled with enemies. There is a nice sense of speed when I dive down and then pull back up, and being able to look around while flying makes the VR setting feel useful rather than just being there for the sake of it. I also like that the environments are destructible, because flying through a battlefield while arrows and attacks are coming towards me gives the experience a little more energy.

The combat is straightforward but enjoyable enough. I have to deal with enemy dragons in the sky as well as archers and other threats around castles and wizard towers. The action is quite fast, so I am spending a lot of time moving around rather than sitting still and aiming at one target. That works well with the flying because the combat and movement are tied together. When I am dodging attacks while trying to line up my own attack, I get a good feeling of actually being on a dragon rather than simply controlling a character who happens to be flying.

The biggest problem for me is the lack of depth. Dragonflight has multiple levels and different environments, but the basic experience does not develop into a proper adventure. I am mainly flying, fighting and moving through the levels, so once I have experienced the main idea there is not much else for me to learn. There are only four Steam achievements as well, which gives me a good indication of how small the overall package is. I think the game would have been much stronger with more missions, different dragon abilities or some kind of progression system that gave me a reason to keep improving.

The VR presentation also shows its age. The game was released in 2017, and while the environments can still look impressive from a distance, some of the assets and effects are fairly basic now. I can see what the developers were aiming for, especially with the huge fantasy environments and dragons filling the sky, but it does not have the level of polish I would expect from a modern VR experience. The movement can also feel a little rough at times, although I think that is partly unavoidable with a game built around constantly flying through the air.

I still think the game is worth trying because it does not ask me to pay anything and it gets straight to its main idea. I do not have to spend hours learning systems before I get to ride the dragon. I can jump in, fly around the world, fight some enemies and experience the main attraction almost immediately. That makes it easy for me to forgive some of the simpler design, especially if I only want a short VR experience rather than a huge game that I can spend dozens of hours playing.

Overall, Dragonflight is a decent little VR experience that succeeds most when I am simply flying through the world on my dragon. The sense of speed, destructible environments and aerial combat give it some genuinely fun moments, and I like how quickly it gets me into the action. The lack of progression, limited content and dated presentation stop it from being something I would come back to constantly, but I think the main idea is still enjoyable. For me, it works best as a short free VR experience that lets me live out the simple fantasy of riding a dragon rather than trying to be a complete game.

Rating: 6.8/10
